chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid; and 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Should a man recite in the first two rak'ahs and in al-'Asr behind the Imam while he does not know whether he is reciting? He said: It is not appropriate for him to recite; he should leave it to the Imam.

key_terms.الْأُولَيَيْنِ: the first two rak'ahs of the prayer
key_terms.خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ: behind the Imam in congregational prayer
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: it is not appropriate or should not be done
key_terms.يَكِلُهُ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ: he leaves the matter of recitation to the Imam

ai.seo_question: Should a person recite behind the Imam in the first two rak'ahs or in al-'Asr prayer if he is unsure whether the Imam is reciting?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of recitation behind the Imam in congregational salat. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that one should not recite in this situation and should entrust the recitation to the Imam, indicating the Imam’s role in leading the prayer.
